chunks: Indeed, the best means by which seekers of nearness to Allah, the Glorified, seek nearness,
is belief in Him and His Prophet, and fighting in His cause, for it is the pinnacle of Islam,
and the Kalimatu'l-Ikhlas (expression of Divine purification) for it is the nature (fitrah),
and the establishment of prayer for it is the religion (millah),
and paying the alms-tax for it is a compulsory obligation,
and fasting the month of Ramadan for it is a shield against chastisement,
and the pilgrimage to the House and its consecration for these two acts banish poverty and wash away sins,
and maintaining kinship for it increases wealth and lengthens life,
and secret alms for it covers shortcomings,
and open alms for it protects against a bad death,
and acts of kindness for it saves from positions of disgrace.
ai.seo_question: What are the best means of seeking nearness to God according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Attributed to Imam Ali in Nahj al-Balagha, this passage presents a comprehensive taxonomy of Islamic practice, elevating faith and jihad as the foundational pillars while detailing the specific spiritual and worldly efficacy of the five pillars and social virtues. It reflects the Shia emphasis on the integration of inner belief (Iman) with outward action (Amal), framing rituals like fasting and pilgrimage not merely as duties but as transformative mechanisms for purification and prosperity. The text underscores the holistic nature of Islam, where private charity and public benevolence are equally vital for maintaining social cohesion and divine favor.
